source.text: וְשָׂרַי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת אַבְרָ֔ם לֹ֥א יָלְדָ֖ה ל֑וֹ וְלָ֛הּ שִׁפְחָ֥ה מִצְרִ֖ית וּשְׁמָ֥הּ הָגָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Sarai, [the] wife of Abram, had not borne to him; and to her [was] a slave woman, Egyptian, and her name [was] Hagar.

en.L: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. She had an Egyptian slave woman whose name was Hagar.
en.B: Sarai, Abram's wife, had still given him no children. But she owned an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
en.R: Abram's wife Sarai still had no children. She had a servant from Egypt named Hagar.

es.L: Y Saray, la mujer de Abram, no le había dado hijos. Ella tenía una esclava egipcia cuyo nombre era Agar.
es.B: Saray, la esposa de Abram, todavía no le había dado hijos. Pero tenía una sierva egipcia llamada Agar.
es.R: Saray, la esposa de Abram, seguía sin tener hijos. Tenía una sierva que había venido de Egipto. Se llamaba Agar.

fr.L: Or Saraï, la femme d’Abram, ne lui avait pas donné d’enfant. Elle avait une esclave égyptienne, dont le nom était Agar.
fr.B: Saraï, la femme d’Abram, ne lui avait toujours pas donné d’enfant. Mais elle avait une servante égyptienne nommée Agar.
fr.R: Saraï, la femme d’Abram, n’avait toujours pas d’enfant. Elle avait une servante qui venait d’Égypte. Elle s’appelait Agar.

sw.L: Na Sarai, mke wa Abramu, alikuwa hajamzalia [mtoto]. Naye alikuwa na mjakazi Mmisri, jina lake Hajiri.
sw.B: Sarai, mke wa Abramu, alikuwa bado hajamzalia mtoto. Lakini alikuwa na mtumishi wa kike Mmisri aitwaye Hajiri.
sw.R: Sarai mke wa Abramu alikuwa bado hana watoto. Alikuwa na mtumishi wa kike kutoka Misri, jina lake Hajiri.

decisions.choice: slave woman: a female slave
decisions.reason: The word (shifchah) means a woman owned by her mistress, a household slave. Hagar may have been acquired in Egypt (12:16).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced in narration ("dit", "prit"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "a donné")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French today. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: mjakazi (L); mtumishi wa kike (B, R); mjakazi at every level in verse 6
decisions.reason: "Mjakazi" is the Swahili word for a female slave, the feminine counterpart of the Pentateuch term "mtumwa" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi wa kike" (or "mtumishi wangu", "wako" where the context shows she is a woman), as the English says "servant". Verse 6 keeps "mjakazi" at every level, as the English keeps "slave".

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֜י אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם הִנֵּה־נָ֞א עֲצָרַ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ מִלֶּ֔דֶת בֹּא־נָא֙ אֶל־שִׁפְחָתִ֔י אוּלַ֥י אִבָּנֶ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נָּהוַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָ֖ם לְק֥וֹל שָׂרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Sarai to Abram, behold, please, has restrained me YHWH from bearing; go, please, in to my slave woman; perhaps I will be built up from her. And listened Abram to [the] voice of Sarai.

en.L: And Sarai said to Abram, "Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept me from bearing children. Please go in to my slave woman; perhaps I shall be built up through her." And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
en.B: Sarai said to Abram, "You see that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not let me bear children. Take my servant; it may be that through her I will have a family." And Abram listened to Sarai.
en.R: So Sarai said to Abram, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not let me have children. Sleep with my servant. Maybe she can have a child for me." Abram agreed to what Sarai said.

es.L: Y dijo Saray a Abram: «Mira, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha impedido dar a luz. Ve, te ruego, y únete a mi esclava; quizá seré edificada por medio de ella». Y escuchó Abram la voz de Saray.
es.B: Saray le dijo a Abram: «Ya ves que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no me ha dejado tener hijos. Toma a mi sierva; tal vez por medio de ella yo tenga familia». Y Abram hizo caso a Saray.
es.R: Entonces Saray le dijo a Abram: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no me ha dejado tener hijos. Acuéstate con mi sierva. Tal vez ella pueda tener un hijo para mí». Abram estuvo de acuerdo con lo que dijo Saray.

fr.L: Et Saraï dit à Abram : « Voici donc, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a empêchée d’enfanter. Va, je te prie, vers mon esclave ; peut-être serai-je bâtie grâce à elle. » Et Abram écouta la voix de Saraï.
fr.B: Saraï dit à Abram : « Tu vois, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne m’a pas permis d’avoir des enfants. Prends ma servante ; peut-être que, grâce à elle, j’aurai une famille. » Et Abram écouta Saraï.
fr.R: Alors Saraï a dit à Abram : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne m’a pas permis d’avoir des enfants. Couche avec ma servante. Elle pourra peut-être avoir un enfant pour moi. » Abram a accepté ce que Saraï proposait.

sw.L: Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "Tazama basi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenizuia nisizae. Tafadhali uingie kwa mjakazi wangu; huenda nitajengwa kupitia yeye." Abramu akaisikiliza sauti ya Sarai.
sw.B: Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "Unaona kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hajaniruhusu kuzaa watoto. Mchukue mtumishi wangu; huenda kupitia yeye nitapata jamaa." Naye Abramu akamsikiliza Sarai.
sw.R: Basi Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hajaniruhusu kupata watoto. Lala na mtumishi wangu. Huenda yeye ataweza kunizalia mtoto." Abramu akakubali alichosema Sarai.

decisions.choice: I shall be built up through her: I shall have children through her
decisions.reason: "Be built up" (ibbaneh) sounds like the word for son (ben): a family is "built" with children (Ruth 4:11).

decisions.choice: go in to my slave woman: the custom of a surrogate mother
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East a childless wife could give her slave to her husband; a child born to the slave counted as the wife's (30:3, 9). The custom is described, not approved.

decisions.choice: Abram listened to the voice of Sarai: the words of 3:17
decisions.reason: The words are those said of the man in 3:17, "you listened to the voice of your wife". Here too a human plan replaces waiting on God's promise (15:4).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: peut-être serai-je bâtie grâce à elle
alternatives: peut-être aurai-je des enfants par elle
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of being "built" (ibbaneh), as the English Literal does, because the word plays on "son" (ben, m1); Balanced and Readable say what it means, a family or a child.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֞ח שָׂרַ֣י אֵֽשֶׁת־אַבְרָ֗ם אֶת־הָגָ֤ר הַמִּצְרִית֙ שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ מִקֵּץ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר שָׁנִ֔ים לְשֶׁ֥בֶת אַבְרָ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְאַבְרָ֥ם אִישָׁ֖הּ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Sarai, [the] wife of Abram, Hagar the Egyptian, her slave woman, at [the] end of ten years of Abram's dwelling in [the] land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to him for a wife.

en.L: So after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her slave woman, and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife.
en.B: Ten years after Abram had settled in Canaan, his wife Sarai gave him Hagar, her Egyptian servant, as a wife.
en.R: Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years. Then Sarai gave her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram to be his second wife.

es.L: Y tomó Saray, la mujer de Abram, a Agar la egipcia, su esclava, al cabo de diez años de habitar Abram en la tierra de Canaán, y se la dio a Abram su marido por mujer.
es.B: Diez años después de que Abram se estableciera en Canaán, su esposa Saray le dio como mujer a Agar, su sierva egipcia.
es.R: Abram llevaba diez años viviendo en Canaán. Entonces Saray le dio a Abram su sierva egipcia, Agar, para que fuera su segunda esposa.

fr.L: Alors Saraï, la femme d’Abram, prit Agar l’Égyptienne, son esclave, au bout de dix ans de séjour d’Abram dans le pays de Canaan, et la donna pour femme à Abram, son mari.
fr.B: Dix ans après qu’Abram s’était établi en Canaan, sa femme Saraï lui donna pour femme Agar, sa servante égyptienne.
fr.R: Abram vivait en Canaan depuis dix ans. Alors Saraï lui a donné sa servante égyptienne, Agar, pour qu’elle soit sa deuxième femme.

sw.L: Basi Sarai, mke wa Abramu, akamchukua Hajiri Mmisri, mjakazi wake, mwisho wa miaka kumi ya Abramu kukaa katika nchi ya Kanaani, akampa Abramu mumewe awe mke wake.
sw.B: Miaka kumi baada ya Abramu kukaa Kanaani, mkewe Sarai alimpa Hajiri, mtumishi wake Mmisri, awe mke wake.
sw.R: Abramu alikuwa ameishi Kanaani kwa miaka kumi. Ndipo Sarai alipompa Abramu mtumishi wake Mmisri Hajiri, awe mke wake wa pili.

decisions.choice: after ten years in Canaan: ten years of waiting
decisions.reason: Abram was seventy-five when he came (12:4); he is now about eighty-five, and the promise of a son seems no nearer.

decisions.choice: as a wife: a secondary wife
decisions.reason: Hagar becomes a wife of lower rank, still Sarai's slave (verse 6).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־הָגָ֖ר וַתַּ֑הַר וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וַתֵּקַ֥ל גְּבִרְתָּ֖הּ בְּעֵינֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived; and she saw that she had conceived, and was slight her mistress in her eyes.

en.L: And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became small in her eyes.
en.B: He slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. Once she knew she was carrying a child, she began to look down on her mistress.
en.R: Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she started to look down on Sarai.

es.L: Y él se unió a Agar, y ella concibió. Y cuando vio que había concebido, su señora se volvió poca cosa a sus ojos.
es.B: Abram tuvo relaciones con Agar, y ella concibió. Cuando supo que estaba esperando un hijo, empezó a despreciar a su señora.
es.R: Abram se acostó con Agar, y ella quedó embarazada. Cuando Agar supo que iba a tener un bebé, empezó a mirar a Saray por encima del hombro.

fr.L: Et il alla vers Agar, et elle conçut. Et quand elle vit qu’elle avait conçu, sa maîtresse devint petite à ses yeux.
fr.B: Il s’unit à Agar, et elle devint enceinte. Dès qu’elle se sut enceinte, elle se mit à mépriser sa maîtresse.
fr.R: Abram a couché avec Agar, et elle est tombée enceinte. Quand Agar a su qu’elle allait avoir un bébé, elle a commencé à regarder Saraï de haut.

sw.L: Akaingia kwa Hajiri, naye akapata mimba. Naye alipoona kwamba amepata mimba, bibi yake akawa mdogo machoni pake.
sw.B: Akalala na Hajiri, naye akapata mimba. Alipojua kwamba ana mimba, akaanza kumdharau bibi yake.
sw.R: Abramu alilala na Hajiri, naye akapata mimba. Hajiri alipojua kwamba atapata mtoto, alianza kumdharau Sarai.

decisions.choice: her mistress became small in her eyes: she despised her
decisions.reason: The verb (qalal) is the one used in 12:3 for treating with contempt. For a barren woman, a pregnant rival in the household was a deep humiliation (1 Samuel 1:6).

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֣י אֶל־אַבְרָם֮ חֲמָסִ֣י עָלֶיךָ֒ אָנֹכִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּי שִׁפְחָתִי֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וָאֵקַ֖ל בְּעֵינֶ֑יהָ יִשְׁפֹּ֥ט יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽיׄךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Sarai to Abram, my wrong [be] on you; I gave my slave woman into your bosom, and she saw that she had conceived, and I became slight in her eyes; may judge YHWH between me and you.

en.L: And Sarai said to Abram, "May the wrong done to me be on you! I gave my slave woman into your arms, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became small in her eyes. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} judge between me and you!"
en.B: Sarai said to Abram, "You are to blame for the wrong done to me! I gave my servant to you, and now that she is pregnant she holds me in contempt. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} be judge between you and me!"
en.R: Then Sarai said to Abram, "This is your fault! I gave my servant to you, and now that she is pregnant, she looks down on me. Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} decide who is right, you or me."

es.L: Y dijo Saray a Abram: «¡Caiga sobre ti el agravio que se me hace! Yo puse a mi esclava en tus brazos, y al ver que había concebido, me volví poca cosa a sus ojos. ¡Juzgue {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entre tú y yo!».
es.B: Saray le dijo a Abram: «¡Tú tienes la culpa de la ofensa que me hacen! Te di a mi sierva, y ahora que está embarazada me desprecia. ¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juzgue entre tú y yo!».
es.R: Entonces Saray le dijo a Abram: «¡Esto es culpa tuya! Te di a mi sierva, y ahora que está embarazada me mira por encima del hombro. Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} decida quién tiene razón, tú o yo».

fr.L: Et Saraï dit à Abram : « Que le tort qui m’est fait retombe sur toi ! J’ai mis mon esclave dans tes bras, et quand elle a vu qu’elle avait conçu, je suis devenue petite à ses yeux. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} juge entre moi et toi ! »
fr.B: Saraï dit à Abram : « C’est toi qui es responsable du tort qu’on me fait ! Je t’ai donné ma servante, et maintenant qu’elle est enceinte, elle me méprise. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit juge entre toi et moi ! »
fr.R: Alors Saraï a dit à Abram : « C’est ta faute ! Je t’ai donné ma servante, et maintenant qu’elle est enceinte, elle me regarde de haut. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} décide qui a raison, toi ou moi. »

sw.L: Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "Dhuluma niliyotendewa na iwe juu yako! Mimi nilimtia mjakazi wangu kifuani mwako, naye alipoona kwamba amepata mimba, nikawa mdogo machoni pake. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ahukumu kati yangu na wewe!"
sw.B: Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "Wewe ndiye wa kulaumiwa kwa dhuluma ninayotendewa! Nilikupa mtumishi wangu, na sasa kwa kuwa ana mimba ananidharau. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na awe mwamuzi kati yako na mimi!"
sw.R: Kisha Sarai akamwambia Abramu, "Hili ni kosa lako! Nilikupa mtumishi wangu, na sasa kwa kuwa ana mimba, ananidharau. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aamue nani yuko sawa, wewe au mimi."

decisions.choice: may the wrong done to me be on you: you are responsible for this
decisions.reason: The word (chamas) is the violence and injustice of 6:11. Sarai holds Abram responsible, as head of the household, for the wrong she suffers.

decisions.choice: may the LORD judge between me and you: let God decide
decisions.reason: An appeal to God as judge in a dispute (31:53; 1 Samuel 24:12).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָ֜ם אֶל־שָׂרַ֗י הִנֵּ֤ה שִׁפְחָתֵךְ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔ךְ עֲשִׂי־לָ֖הּ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יִךְ וַתְּעַנֶּ֣הָ שָׂרַ֔י וַתִּבְרַ֖ח מִפָּנֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abram to Sarai, behold, your slave woman [is] in your hand; do to her the good in your eyes. And afflicted her Sarai, and she fled from her face.

en.L: And Abram said to Sarai, "Look, your slave woman is in your power; do to her whatever is good in your eyes." Then Sarai afflicted her, and she fled from her.
en.B: Abram answered Sarai, "She is your slave, and she is in your hands. Deal with her as you see fit." Then Sarai treated her so harshly that she ran away.
en.R: Abram answered Sarai, "She is your slave. Do whatever you think is best." Then Sarai was so cruel to Hagar that Hagar ran away.

es.L: Y dijo Abram a Saray: «Mira, tu esclava está en tu mano; haz con ella lo que es bueno a tus ojos». Y Saray la oprimió, y ella huyó de delante de ella.
es.B: Abram le respondió a Saray: «Es tu esclava, y está en tus manos. Trátala como te parezca». Entonces Saray la trató con tanta dureza que ella se escapó.
es.R: Abram le respondió a Saray: «Es tu esclava. Haz lo que creas mejor». Entonces Saray fue tan cruel con Agar que Agar se escapó.

fr.L: Et Abram dit à Saraï : « Voici, ton esclave est entre tes mains ; fais-lui ce qui est bon à tes yeux. » Alors Saraï l’opprima, et elle s’enfuit loin d’elle.
fr.B: Abram répondit à Saraï : « C’est ton esclave, elle est en ton pouvoir. Traite-la comme bon te semble. » Alors Saraï la traita si durement qu’elle s’enfuit.
fr.R: Abram a répondu à Saraï : « C’est ton esclave. Fais ce que tu penses être le mieux. » Alors Saraï a été si méchante avec Agar qu’Agar s’est enfuie.

sw.L: Abramu akamwambia Sarai, "Tazama, mjakazi wako yu mkononi mwako; mtendee lililo jema machoni pako." Sarai akamtesa, naye akamkimbia.
sw.B: Abramu akamjibu Sarai, "Yeye ni mjakazi wako, na yuko chini ya mamlaka yako. Mtendee unavyoona inafaa." Ndipo Sarai akamtendea kwa ukali mpaka akakimbia.
sw.R: Abramu akamjibu Sarai, "Yeye ni mjakazi wako. Fanya lolote unaloona ni bora." Ndipo Sarai akamtesa Hajiri vibaya sana, hata Hajiri akakimbia.

decisions.choice: afflicted: oppressed, mistreated
decisions.reason: The verb (innah) is the one used in 15:13 of Egypt afflicting Israel. Here an Egyptian slave is afflicted by the mother of Israel. The text does not excuse it.

decisions.choice: your slave is in your power: Abram steps back
decisions.reason: Abram leaves Hagar to Sarai, though Hagar is carrying his child. Neither he nor Sarai comes out of the episode well.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where ownership is the point: Abram hands Hagar back to Sarai as her property, to deal with as she likes (m2).

decisions.choice: l'opprima (L); la traita si durement (B); a été si méchante (R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "opprimer", the verb French uses for Egypt oppressing Israel, so the echo of 15:13 the meaning decision points to (m1) can be heard; Balanced and Readable say how she treated her.

source.text: וַֽיִּמְצָאָ֞הּ מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה עַל־עֵ֥ין הַמַּ֖יִם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַל־הָעַ֖יִן בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ שֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And found her [the] angel of YHWH by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on [the] way to Shur.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, the spring on the road to Shur.
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came upon her beside a spring in the desert, the spring on the road to Shur.
en.R: Near a spring in the desert, on the road to Shur, the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} found Hagar.

es.L: Y la halló el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} junto a una fuente de agua en el desierto, junto a la fuente que está en el camino de Sur.
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encontró con ella junto a un manantial en el desierto, el manantial que está en el camino a Sur.
es.R: Cerca de un manantial en el desierto, en el camino a Sur, el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} encontró a Agar.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} la trouva près d’une source d’eau dans le désert, près de la source sur le chemin de Shour.
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} la rencontra près d’une source dans le désert, la source qui est sur la route de Shour.
fr.R: Près d’une source dans le désert, sur la route de Shour, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a trouvé Agar.

sw.L: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamkuta karibu na chemchemi ya maji jangwani, chemchemi iliyo njiani kwenda Shuri.
sw.B: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamkuta kando ya chemchemi jangwani, ile chemchemi iliyo kwenye barabara ya kwenda Shuri.
sw.R: Karibu na chemchemi moja jangwani, njiani kwenda Shuri, malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimkuta Hajiri.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: God's messenger, who speaks as God himself
alternatives: an ordinary angel, distinct from God
decisions.reason: "Angel" means messenger. The angel of the LORD appears here for the first time. He speaks as God (verse 10, "I will multiply"), and Hagar says she has seen God (verse 13). The text does not explain how the messenger and the LORD are related; Christian readers have often seen him as a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son.

decisions.choice: the road to Shur: the way back to Egypt
decisions.reason: Shur lay on Egypt's eastern border (25:18). Hagar is heading home.

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר הָגָ֞ר שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרַ֛י אֵֽי־מִזֶּ֥ה בָ֖את וְאָ֣נָה תֵלֵ֑כִי וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִפְּנֵי֙ שָׂרַ֣י גְּבִרְתִּ֔י אָנֹכִ֖י בֹּרַֽחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Hagar, slave woman of Sarai, from where have you come and where are you going? And she said, from [the] face of Sarai my mistress I am fleeing.

en.L: And he said, "Hagar, slave woman of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" And she said, "I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai."
en.B: He asked her, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you headed?" She answered, "I am running away from Sarai, my mistress."
en.R: He said, "Hagar, Sarai's servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I am running away from Sarai, the woman I belong to."

es.L: Y dijo: «Agar, esclava de Saray, ¿de dónde vienes y adónde vas?». Y ella dijo: «Huyo de delante de Saray, mi señora».
es.B: Él le preguntó: «Agar, sierva de Saray, ¿de dónde vienes y hacia dónde te diriges?». Ella respondió: «Estoy huyendo de Saray, mi señora».
es.R: Él le dijo: «Agar, sierva de Saray, ¿de dónde vienes y adónde vas?». Ella le contestó: «Me estoy escapando de Saray, la mujer a la que pertenezco».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Agar, esclave de Saraï, d’où viens-tu, et où vas-tu ? » Et elle dit : « Je fuis loin de Saraï, ma maîtresse. »
fr.B: Il lui demanda : « Agar, servante de Saraï, d’où viens-tu et où vas-tu ? » Elle répondit : « Je m’enfuis loin de Saraï, ma maîtresse. »
fr.R: Il lui a dit : « Agar, servante de Saraï, d’où viens-tu, et où vas-tu ? » Elle a répondu : « Je me sauve loin de Saraï, la femme à qui j’appartiens. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Hajiri, mjakazi wa Sarai, umetoka wapi, nawe unakwenda wapi?" Akasema, "Ninakimbia mbele ya bibi yangu Sarai."
sw.B: Akamwuliza, "Hajiri, mtumishi wa Sarai, unatoka wapi, na unaelekea wapi?" Akajibu, "Ninamkimbia Sarai, bibi yangu."
sw.R: Akamwambia, "Hajiri, mtumishi wa Sarai, umetoka wapi, na unakwenda wapi?" Akajibu, "Ninamkimbia Sarai, bibi ambaye mimi ni mali yake."

decisions.choice: Hagar: God's messenger calls her by name
decisions.reason: Abram and Sarai never use Hagar's name; the angel does. God sees and knows the slave woman.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה שׁ֖וּבִי אֶל־גְּבִרְתֵּ֑ךְ וְהִתְעַנִּ֖י תַּ֥חַת יָדֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her [the] angel of YHWH, return to your mistress and submit yourself under her hands.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "Return to your mistress and submit to her authority."
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "Go back to your mistress and put yourself under her authority."
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "Go back to Sarai and obey her."

es.L: Y le dijo el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: «Vuelve a tu señora y humíllate bajo sus manos».
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo: «Regresa con tu señora y ponte bajo su autoridad».
es.R: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo: «Vuelve con Saray y obedécela».

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui dit : « Retourne vers ta maîtresse, et humilie-toi sous ses mains. »
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui dit : « Retourne chez ta maîtresse et soumets-toi à son autorité. »
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui a dit : « Retourne chez Saraï et obéis-lui. »

sw.L: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Rudi kwa bibi yako, ujinyenyekeze chini ya mikono yake."
sw.B: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Rudi kwa bibi yako, ujiweke chini ya mamlaka yake."
sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Rudi kwa Sarai, umtii."

decisions.choice: submit: humble yourself
decisions.reason: The verb is related to "afflicted" in verse 6: Hagar is to accept a lowly place. The command comes with a promise (verses 10-12), which makes the return bearable.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הַרְבָּ֥ה אַרְבֶּ֖ה אֶת־זַרְעֵ֑ךְ וְלֹ֥א יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her [the] angel of YHWH, increasing I will increase your offspring, and not it will be counted for multitude.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they cannot be counted for multitude."
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} also said, "I will make your descendants so many that no one will be able to count them."
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} also said, "I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them."

es.L: Y le dijo el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: «Haré muy numerosa tu descendencia, tanto que por su gran número no se podrá contar».
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} añadió: «Tendrás tantos descendientes que nadie podrá contarlos».
es.R: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} también le dijo: «Te daré tantos descendientes que nadie los podrá contar».

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui dit : « Je multiplierai grandement ta descendance, et on ne pourra pas la compter, tant elle sera nombreuse. »
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ajouta : « Je rendrai tes descendants si nombreux que personne ne pourra les compter. »
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a dit encore : « Je te donnerai tellement de descendants que personne ne pourra les compter. »

sw.L: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Hakika nitauongeza sana uzao wako, hata hautahesabika kwa wingi wake."
sw.B: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaongeza kusema, "Nitawafanya wazao wako kuwa wengi mno hata hakuna atakayeweza kuwahesabu."
sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema pia, "Nitakupa wazao wengi sana, hata hakuna mtu atakayeweza kuwahesabu."

decisions.choice: I will multiply: a promise like Abram's, given to a woman
decisions.reason: The angel speaks as God ("I"), and gives Hagar a promise like those given to Abram (13:16; 15:5). She is the only woman in Genesis to receive such a promise directly.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן וְקָרָ֤את שְׁמוֹ֙ יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־עָנְיֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her [the] angel of YHWH, behold, you [are] pregnant and will bear a son, and you will call his name Ishmael, for has heard YHWH your affliction.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "Look, you are pregnant and will bear a son, and you shall call his name Ishmael, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has heard your affliction.
en.B: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "You are with child, and you will have a son. Call him Ishmael, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has listened to your suffering.
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "You are going to have a son. Name him Ishmael, which means 'God hears,' because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has heard how much you have suffered.

es.L: Y le dijo el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: «Mira, estás encinta y darás a luz un hijo, y le pondrás el nombre de Ismael, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha escuchado tu aflicción.
es.B: Luego el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo: «Estás embarazada y tendrás un hijo. Ponle por nombre Ismael, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha prestado oído a tu sufrimiento.
es.R: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo: «Vas a tener un hijo. Llámalo Ismael, que quiere decir “Dios oye”, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha oído cuánto has sufrido.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui dit : « Voici, tu es enceinte, et tu enfanteras un fils, et tu l’appelleras du nom d’Ismaël, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a entendu ton affliction.
fr.B: Puis l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dit : « Tu es enceinte, et tu auras un fils. Tu l’appelleras Ismaël, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a entendu ta souffrance.
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a dit : « Tu vas avoir un fils. Appelle-le Ismaël, ce qui veut dire “Dieu entend”, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a entendu combien tu as souffert.

sw.L: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Tazama, una mimba, nawe utazaa mwana, nawe utamwita jina lake Ishmaeli, kwa kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesikia mateso yako.
sw.B: Kisha malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Wewe una mimba, nawe utapata mwana. Umwite Ishmaeli, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesikiliza mateso yako.
sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Utapata mtoto wa kiume. Mwite Ishmaeli, maana yake 'Mungu husikia,' kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesikia jinsi ulivyoteseka sana.

decisions.choice: Ishmael: "God hears"
decisions.reason: The name means "God hears", and the reason is that the LORD has heard Hagar's affliction, the word of verse 6. God hears the oppressed, as later he hears Israel in Egypt (Exodus 3:7).

decisions.choice: which means 'God hears'
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name so the reason given makes sense (m1).

source.text: וְה֤וּא יִהְיֶה֙ פֶּ֣רֶא אָדָ֔ם יָד֣וֹ בַכֹּ֔ל וְיַ֥ד כֹּ֖ל בּ֑וֹ וְעַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־אֶחָ֖יו יִשְׁכֹּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand against everyone, and [the] hand of everyone against him; and over against all his brothers he will dwell.

en.L: And he will be a wild donkey of a man, his hand against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he will dwell over against all his brothers."
en.B: He will be like a wild donkey: he will raise his hand against everyone, and everyone will raise a hand against him, and he will live at odds with all his kin."
en.R: Your son will be like a wild donkey, free and hard to control. He will fight with everyone, and everyone will fight with him. He will live apart from all his relatives."

es.L: Y él será un hombre [como] asno salvaje; su mano [estará] contra todos, y la mano de todos contra él, y habitará frente a todos sus hermanos».
es.B: Será como un asno salvaje: levantará la mano contra todos, y todos levantarán la mano contra él, y vivirá enfrentado a todos sus parientes».
es.R: Tu hijo será como un burro salvaje, libre y difícil de controlar. Peleará con todos, y todos pelearán con él. Vivirá apartado de todos sus parientes».

fr.L: Et lui sera un homme [semblable à un] âne sauvage : sa main contre tous, et la main de tous contre lui ; et il habitera face à tous ses frères. »
fr.B: Il sera comme un âne sauvage : il lèvera la main contre tous, et tous lèveront la main contre lui, et il vivra en conflit avec tous ses frères. »
fr.R: Ton fils sera comme un âne sauvage, libre et difficile à dompter. Il se battra contre tout le monde, et tout le monde se battra contre lui. Il vivra loin de tous les gens de sa famille. »

sw.L: Naye atakuwa mtu [kama] punda-mwitu; mkono wake [utakuwa] juu ya kila mtu, na mkono wa kila mtu juu yake; naye atakaa kuwakabili ndugu zake wote."
sw.B: Atakuwa kama punda-mwitu: atainua mkono dhidi ya kila mtu, na kila mtu atainua mkono dhidi yake, naye ataishi akishindana na jamaa zake wote."
sw.R: Mwanao atakuwa kama punda-mwitu, huru na mgumu kutawaliwa. Atapigana na kila mtu, na kila mtu atapigana naye. Ataishi mbali na ndugu zake wote."

decisions.choice: a wild donkey of a man: free and untamed
decisions.reason: The wild donkey of the desert is a picture of untamed freedom (Job 39:5-8). The words describe a free, roaming life, not simply an insult.

decisions.choice: he will dwell over against all his brothers: in hostility, or to the east of them
alternatives: he will live to the east of all his brothers
decisions.reason: The phrase "over against the face of" can mean in defiance of, or opposite, that is, east of. The Ishmaelites lived in the desert east and south of Israel (25:18).

decisions.choice: un hombre [como] asno salvaje
decisions.reason: Spanish cannot copy the Hebrew "a wild donkey of a man"; Literal supplies the comparison in brackets. "Asno salvaje" names the animal of the desert (m1); Readable says "burro salvaje", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: un homme [semblable à un] âne sauvage
decisions.reason: French cannot copy the Hebrew "a wild donkey of a man" as English can; Literal supplies the comparison in brackets. "Âne sauvage" is used rather than the rarer "onagre".

decisions.choice: mtu [kama] punda-mwitu
decisions.reason: Swahili cannot copy the Hebrew "a wild donkey of a man"; Literal supplies the comparison in brackets.

source.text: וַתִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־יְהוָה֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל רֳאִ֑י כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה הֲגַ֥ם הֲלֹ֛ם רָאִ֖יתִי אַחֲרֵ֥י רֹאִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she called [the] name of YHWH who spoke to her, you [are] a God of seeing; for she said, have I also here seen after [the one who] sees me?

en.L: And she called the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who spoke to her, "You are a God who sees," for she said, "Have I really seen here the one who sees me?"
en.B: So she gave this name to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who had spoken to her: "You are the God who sees me." For she said, "Have I truly seen the One who watches over me?"
en.R: Hagar gave a name to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who had spoken to her. She called {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} "the God who sees me." She said, "I have seen the One who sees me!"

es.L: Y llamó el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que le hablaba: «Tú eres un Dios que ve», porque dijo: «¿De veras he visto aquí al que me ve?».
es.B: Entonces dio este nombre {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que le había hablado: «Tú eres el Dios que me ve». Porque dijo: «¿De verdad he visto al que vela por mí?».
es.R: Agar dio un nombre {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que le había hablado. Ella {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llamó «el Dios que me ve». Y dijo: «¡He visto al que me ve!».

fr.L: Et elle appela le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui lui parlait : « Tu es un Dieu qui voit », car elle dit : « Ai-je vraiment vu ici celui qui me voit ? »
fr.B: Elle donna alors ce nom {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} qui lui avait parlé : « Tu es le Dieu qui me voit. » Car elle disait : « Ai-je vraiment vu Celui qui veille sur moi ? »
fr.R: Agar a donné un nom {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} qui lui avait parlé. Elle {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a appelé « le Dieu qui me voit ». Elle a dit : « J’ai vu Celui qui me voit ! »

sw.L: Naye akaliita jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyesema naye, "Wewe ni Mungu aonaye," kwa maana alisema, "Je, kweli nimemwona hapa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeniona?"
sw.B: Basi akampa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyesema naye jina hili: "Wewe ndiwe Mungu anayeniona." Kwa maana alisema, "Je, kweli nimemwona {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayenilinda?"
sw.R: Hajiri alimpa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyesema naye jina. Alimwita "Mungu anayeniona." Akasema, "Nimemwona {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeniona!"

decisions.choice: a God who sees: El Roi
alternatives: a God of seeing (who lets himself be seen)
decisions.reason: Hagar is the only person in the Bible who gives God a name. El Roi can mean "the God who sees me" or "the God of my seeing", that is, whom I have seen. God has seen her affliction (verse 11).

decisions.choice: have I really seen here the one who sees me?: an obscure line
alternatives: have I seen here the back of the one who sees me?
have I lived after seeing God?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is difficult. It may express wonder that she has seen God and lived (32:30; Exodus 33:20-23), or that she has seen him "after" he saw her.

decisions.choice: You (at the start of a sentence)
decisions.reason: "You" addressed to God begins the sentence here and so is capitalised either way; Readable uses "him" under the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeniona (L, R), anayenilinda (B); no span at Readable "Alimwita"
alternatives: no span, as the English "the one who sees me"
decisions.reason: Swahili needs a free pronoun "yeye" for "the one who sees me", and a free pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun span; the English Readable "him" is only a prefix in "alimwita", which cannot take a capital, so it has none.

source.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ קָרָ֣א לַבְּאֵ֔ר בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י הִנֵּ֥ה בֵין־קָדֵ֖שׁ וּבֵ֥ין בָּֽרֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore one called the well Beer-lahai-roi; behold, [it is] between Kadesh and Bered.

en.L: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; it is between Kadesh and Bered.
en.B: That is why the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is still there, between Kadesh and Bered.
en.R: That is why the well is called Beer-lahai-roi, which means "the well of the Living One who sees me." It is between Kadesh and Bered.

es.L: Por eso se llamó el pozo Beer-lajai-roi; he aquí, [está] entre Cades y Bered.
es.B: Por esta razón el pozo se llamó Beer-lajai-roi. Todavía está allí, entre Cades y Bered.
es.R: Por eso el pozo se llama Beer-lajai-roi, que quiere decir «el pozo del Viviente que me ve». Está entre Cades y Bered.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi on appela le puits Beer-Lahaï-Roï ; voici, il est entre Kadesh et Béred.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi ce puits fut appelé Beer-Lahaï-Roï. Il se trouve encore là, entre Kadesh et Béred.
fr.R: C’est pour cela qu’on appelle ce puits Beer-Lahaï-Roï, ce qui veut dire « le puits du Vivant qui me voit ». Il se trouve entre Kadesh et Béred.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo kisima kile kikaitwa Beer-lahai-roi; tazama, [kiko] kati ya Kadeshi na Beredi.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu kisima hicho kiliitwa Beer-lahai-roi. Bado kipo, kati ya Kadeshi na Beredi.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu kisima hicho kinaitwa Beer-lahai-roi, maana yake "kisima cha Aliye Hai anayeniona." Kiko kati ya Kadeshi na Beredi.

decisions.choice: Beer-lahai-roi: "the well of the Living One who sees me"
decisions.reason: The name gathers up Hagar's words: the God who sees her is alive. Isaac later lives near this well (24:62; 25:11).

decisions.choice: It is still there
decisions.reason: "Behold" points to the well as still known in the narrator's day; Balanced says so.

source.text: וַתֵּ֧לֶד הָגָ֛ר לְאַבְרָ֖ם בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָ֧ם שֶׁם־בְּנ֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה הָגָ֖ר יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל׃

records.literal_gloss: And bore Hagar to Abram a son, and called Abram [the] name of his son whom bore Hagar Ishmael.

en.L: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
en.B: So Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named the son she had borne him Ishmael.
en.R: Hagar gave birth to Abram's son, and Abram named him Ishmael.

es.L: Y Agar dio a luz un hijo a Abram, y Abram puso a su hijo, el que Agar había dado a luz, el nombre de Ismael.
es.B: Así Agar le dio un hijo a Abram, y Abram llamó Ismael al hijo que ella le había dado.
es.R: Agar tuvo un hijo de Abram, y Abram le puso por nombre Ismael.

fr.L: Et Agar enfanta un fils à Abram, et Abram appela du nom d’Ismaël son fils qu’Agar avait enfanté.
fr.B: Agar donna donc un fils à Abram, et Abram appela Ismaël le fils qu’elle lui avait donné.
fr.R: Agar a mis au monde le fils d’Abram, et Abram l’a appelé Ismaël.

sw.L: Hajiri akamzalia Abramu mwana, naye Abramu akamwita mwanawe, ambaye Hajiri alimzaa, jina lake Ishmaeli.
sw.B: Basi Hajiri akamzalia Abramu mwana, naye Abramu akampa mwana huyo aliyezaliwa na Hajiri jina Ishmaeli.
sw.R: Hajiri alimzalia Abramu mtoto wa kiume, naye Abramu akamwita Ishmaeli.

decisions.choice: Abram named him Ishmael: the name the angel gave
decisions.reason: Abram gives the name the angel told Hagar (verse 11), so Hagar must have told him of the encounter.

source.text: וְאַבְרָ֕ם בֶּן־שְׁמֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים בְּלֶֽדֶת־הָגָ֥ר אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל לְאַבְרָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Abram [was] a son of eighty years and six years when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

en.L: And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
en.B: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.
en.R: Abram was eighty-six years old when Ishmael was born.

es.L: Y Abram tenía ochenta y seis años cuando Agar le dio a luz a Ismael.
es.B: Abram tenía ochenta y seis años cuando Agar le dio a Ismael.
es.R: Abram tenía ochenta y seis años cuando nació Ismael.

fr.L: Et Abram était âgé de quatre-vingt-six ans quand Agar enfanta Ismaël à Abram.
fr.B: Abram avait quatre-vingt-six ans quand Agar lui donna Ismaël.
fr.R: Abram avait quatre-vingt-six ans quand Ismaël est né.

sw.L: Naye Abramu alikuwa na umri wa miaka themanini na sita Hajiri alipomzalia Abramu Ishmaeli.
sw.B: Abramu alikuwa na miaka themanini na sita Hajiri alipomzalia Ishmaeli.
sw.R: Abramu alikuwa na umri wa miaka themanini na sita Ishmaeli alipozaliwa.
